request.subject: Both Engines Died Over New York City - part 3: The Simulator Tests That Questioned Sully
request.title: Both Engines Died Over New York City (Part 3/3)
request.description:
Simulator pilots sometimes made it back to a runway, until investigators added time to think. The movie Sully turned those tests into drama. Did the captain make the right call?

Part 3 of 3: Both Engines Died Over New York City

Sources:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Airways_Flight_1549
https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/AccidentReports/Reports/AAR1003.pdf
https://flightsafety.org/asw-article/survival-on-the-hudson/

Stock footage: Pexels. Made with AI-assisted narration.

#shorts #truestory

extra_params.video_script: Computer tests later suggested the jet might have reached an airport. In Part 2, all 155 people survived a Hudson River landing. Pilots flew the same emergency in flight simulators. About half of them made it back to a runway. But they turned back instantly, with no time to think. When investigators added about half a minute for thinking, the simulated flight crashed. They concluded the river gave everyone the best chance to survive. The movie Sully later built its drama around those tests. The runway nobody would pick was the right one. Subscribe for a new true story every day.
